name: Lang'e
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Retired Glottolog entry: likely duplicate of Talu (yta) or Lhao Vo (mhx); no distinct language documented

sources.citation: 胡素华 & 段秋红 (Hu Suhua & Duan Qiuhong). 2021. 彝语他留话四音格词的韵律和语义特征 [Prosodic and semantic features of tetrasyllabic words in Taliu Yi]. 民族语文 2021(6): 27-36.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing about Talu/Lang'e stress; '重音' appears once, inside a generic definition of 韵律 quoted from 周志培 2003 (p.27). Gives Talu 40 initials, 70 finals, tone sandhi in four-syllable words. Talu is the variety Glottolog equates with Lang'e.

sources.citation: Yang, Cathryn; Kwok Wailing 范秀琳; Zhou Decai 周德才; Yang Wenjing 杨文静. 2017. 滇西北彝语他留土语群：忠诚的南诏战士 / The Taloid cluster of Northwestern Yunnan. ICSTLL-50, Beijing (slides; academia.edu page text).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Lists 崀峨/拉务 as Taloid member no. 2 with wordlist source '陈康 2011'; historical-dialectology classification only.

sources.citation: Lewis, Simons & Fennig (eds). 2016. Ethnologue 19, entry Lang'e [yne] (Internet Archive copy).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; no Typology field. Alt name La'u, 2,000 (2007), SW Yongsheng, Ngwi Central, status 6a.

sources.citation: Lama, Ziwo Qiu-Fuyuan. 2012. Subgrouping of Nisoic (Yi) Languages: A Study from the Perspectives of Shared Innovation and Phylogenetic Estimation. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Arlington. 399 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: online with a university library login
sources.note: Nothing (0 hits for stress/accent in the full text). p.53 lists Lang'e (or La'u) among Bradley's Central Ngwi; Lavu 拉乌 profile (pp. c.94-95): 37 initials, 29 vowels, 4 tones /55/ /33/ /13/ /21/ from YYFC 1983; Table 5.1 gives the Lavu data point as 云南省永胜县星湖公社崀峩大队王家村 (Wangjia village, Lang'e brigade), i.e. Lavu = Lang'e.

sources.note: Nothing. Only names (Lang'e, La'u), population 2,000, location (SW Yongsheng County), classification Central Ngwi; sole cited source Bradley 2007 Atlas + personal communication.
